purpose: Behavior cases for sparse priority, status, relationship, and archive-candidate title semantics.

cases.input: Three current tasks are unfinished: database reconciliation risks losing recoverable history, an implementation has a routine next feature, and a migration awaits a non-urgent choice. The full accessible scope was reviewed.
Three current unfinished tasks are equally actionable, and the reviewed bodies provide no owner urgency, risk, blocking, or time-sensitivity distinction.
The accessible inventory contains one urgent unfinished task, but several related current tasks are inaccessible and could outrank it.

expected.reason: Coverage is insufficient for a credible global comparison

cases.input: Task A currently has red, task B is the proposed new winner, and A's title changes after the manifest freezes but before mutation.
Old red removal succeeded and the scope has zero red, but the proposed winner's live title changed before red could be added.
Final verification finds two red tasks, but the proposed winner's live title no longer matches the exact red title applied by this transition.
One task names an exact next implementation step; another merely says improvements may be possible someday.
A migration awaits owner approval. A recovery task cannot continue because its database is locked and needs remediation.
A task is waiting on a named external approval and cannot progress until that response arrives; it is not technically broken and is not complete.
A task is blocked by an unexplained external failure, and the reviewed body identifies no remediation, decision, or concrete next action.
A verified architecture decision is still authoritative. A separate verified one-off availability check has no remaining work or durable reference value.
A delivered one-off research answer has no stated remaining work, but the body and related tasks do not establish whether its result remains useful.
An older plan was explicitly replaced by named task T2. A different old plan only resembles recent work with no successor evidence.
A thirty-day-old task remains the only source for an unfinished migration.
Crest research pruning is complete and directly verified; project and cleanup symbols are useful and no cross-task marker applies.
One task is the red winner, has a concrete owner decision, is canonical, belongs to project 🌊, is implementation work, and is waiting for approval; all six marker dimensions have evidence.
